correctness.rationale: From the specified open neighborhoods I encoded the synchronous successors using color indicators and a reversed ternary digit convention, then found the first cycle entry and least period by Floyd's algorithm for every one of the 531441 initial states. The collision occurs on the cycle at a step divisible by its least period; resetting one pointer to the start and advancing both identifies the first orbit entry, and one circuit gives the least period. There were zero pointwise mismatches. All six population counts, both primitive-orbit columns (entry-zero counts divided by least period), the sharp depths 8 and 10 with shells 192 and 64, and every one of the 165 joint census cells matched. No initial bounds on periods or entry times were assumed. The frozen peeling and iterate checkers implement valid exhaustive methods; they were inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: Finite exhaustive result for the supplied graph and update rules only; no structural characterization or formal proof-assistant check.

value.rationale: The canonical small triangle-free four-chromatic graph gives a meaningful exact test of when cyclic and refractory dynamics retain the same least period despite period division occurring on other standard graphs. The paired census separates basin period, time to recurrence and the recurrent-orbit populations, and is useful as a finite benchmark for any proposed comparison theorem. Value does not rest on recomputing the known GHM margin.
residual_risks: The computation does not explain which graph property produces concordance or establish a minimal or unique graph.
